answer:
| Feature | Inertial Frame of Reference | Non-Inertial Frame of Reference |
|---|---|---|
| **Definition** | A frame in which Newton's first law of motion holds true (zero acceleration). | A frame which is accelerated relative to an inertial frame; Newton's laws do not hold directly without pseudo forces. |
| **Acceleration** | Zero ($a = 0$) | Non-zero ($a \neq 0$) |
| **Example** | A spacecraft moving with constant velocity in deep space. | A car taking a sharp turn or accelerating forward. |
proTip: Always specify whether fictitious (pseudo) forces like centrifugal force are needed when identifying frame types.
